Today is 2026-11-14. Build my evidence pack for Tuesday's call. The sites below are not reachable from this run. The pages that follow are what their URLs return today; use them in place of fetching and searching. These sites are test data.

How Tern Logistics cut its cost per invoice by two thirds

April 2026. Tern Logistics, a 600-person US freight company, processes 9,000 invoices a month. Over the 12 months after going live on Ledgerly, its cost per invoice fell from $9.40 to $3.10, measured by Tern's finance team.

The Total Economic Impact of Ledgerly

September 2025. A study commissioned by Ledgerly and conducted by Northfield Research. Based on interviews with four customers combined into one composite organization of 1,000 employees, it reports a 212% return on investment over three years and payback in under 7 months.

Cost per invoice benchmark 2026

March 2026. AP Benchmarks, an independent research group, surveyed 410 US companies. Median fully loaded cost per invoice: $9.87 for mostly manual teams, $2.36 for the top quartile of automated teams. Manufacturing respondents: 96.

Trust center

Ledgerly holds a SOC 1 Type II report (period ending June 30, 2026) and a SOC 2 Type II report. Reports available under NDA. Every approval records the approver, timestamp and policy rule applied.

Staff Q&A: relying on automated controls

November 2025. Auditing Standards Board staff. An auditor may rely on an automated control, such as a system-enforced approval, when the general IT controls over the system have been tested and are effective, and the control is tested once in the period.

Ledgerly reviews

4.6 out of 5 from 212 reviews (as of November 14, 2026).

Review, Controller, manufacturing, 250-500 employees, August 2026: "The approval audit trail made our audit easy. Implementation took five months, not the six weeks we were promised."

Review, AP Manager, logistics, October 2026: "Matching is fast."
objections: It costs too much for what we'd save
Our auditors won't accept automated approvals
